correctness.rationale: The linear part cancels and the quadratic block enters only through B. The cubic monomial is the indicator of h. Its seed polar rows are empty for 0, U minus {0,h} for h, and {h,h+a} for each other nonzero a. Among the 56 ordered distinct seed pairs, 14 involving h have symmetric difference 6 and the other 42 have difference 2. Among the 42 ordered distinct nonzero seed pairs, six directed differences from h to a in U minus {0,h} have size 5 and the rest have size 1. For distinct nonzero W coordinates, two independent symplectic equations give Q/4 solutions for each of 8 choices of the seed coordinate of the witness. Equal nonzero W coordinates impose a common equation of rank one on precisely the seed symmetric difference. With one W coordinate zero, the free seed choices are one row or its complement and the nonzero equation gives Q/2 solutions per choice. With both zero, each directed difference contributes Q times its size. The cases respectively give 64(Q−1)(Q−2) at 2Q; 42(Q−1) at Q and 14(Q−1) at 3Q; 48(Q−1) at Q and 8(Q−1) at 3Q; 8(Q−1) at Q and 48(Q−1) at 3Q; and 36 at Q and 6 at 5Q. They sum to (8Q−1)(8Q−2). Q is attained already among seed-only pairs; the six maxima and the limiting fraction follow, and m=1 keeps all four strata nonempty. An independent finite reconstruction from signed row correlations reproduced all three histograms and the six maximum pairs in each dimension.
residual_risks: The finite replay uses a standard symplectic coordinate form and corroborates but does not extend the all-m argument. Nondegeneracy over F2 and the ordered pair exclusions are essential in the derivation.

value.rationale: The exact spectrum answers a natural robustness question for a published existence construction: every pair has witness density at least 1/8, almost every ordered pair has density 1/4, and the six extreme pairs are identified. This separates typical from worst-case behavior at every allowed dimension and sharpens existence without claiming novelty for the form.
residual_risks: This is a quantitative result for one structured family; it gives no robustness theorem for arbitrary ordered-separating cubics.
